subject: physics
question_text: Derive Kepler’s third law of planetary motion from Newton’s law of gravitation, for a planet moving in a circular orbit.

verification.note: PREDICTED — Session 89 enumeration sweep (archetype × object grid over the NCERT chapter): this question has not appeared in any paper or source book we hold, but the chapter contains it and the 2-mark/4-mark format admits it. Authored as a lean card; promote to a full card when a paper season or a Telangana IPE teacher validates the cell. Split invented, as everywhere.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: The circular orbit
lines: Take a planet of mass m moving in a circular
orbit of radius r about the sun of mass M. The
sun’s pull supplies the centripetal force:

lines.text: m v² / r = G M m / r²

lines: Cancelling m and one factor of r,
steps.why: A circle is not the real orbit, but Kepler’s third law comes out with the semi-major axis in place of r — so the circle gives the right law.
common_mistakes: Keeping the planet’s mass m in the result; it cancels at this very first step.

recall.must_convey: That equating the gravitational pull to the centripetal force gives v squared equals G M by r.
accept: v squared is G M by r
reject: T squared is proportional to r cubed

steps.memory_tip: Set the pull equal to mv²/r, cancel m and one r, and v² = GM/r is left.
steps.margin_note: Two marks. The force balance and the cancelling belong on separate lines.

steps.label: The result
lines: The time period is T = 2πr / v, so

lines.text: T² = (4π² / G M) r³,   so   T² ∝ r³

lines: The bracket 4π²/GM is the same for every planet
of the sun, which is why one constant serves
steps.why: The constant depends on the mass of the CENTRAL body only — which is how the law is used to measure the mass of the sun, and the masses of planets from their moons.
common_mistakes: Claiming the constant is universal; it changes if the central body changes.

recall.must_convey: That T squared equals four pi squared by G M times r cubed, so T squared is proportional to r cubed.
accept: T squared proportional to r cubed
four pi squared by G M
reject: v squared is G M by r

steps.memory_tip: T = 2πr/v gives r² on top and GM/r underneath, so the r powers add to r³.
steps.margin_note: The last two marks. Substitute v, box T² ∝ r³, then name M in the constant.

insider_note: Half the marks are in the setup, so write the pull equal to the centripetal force before going on to T² ∝ r³.
